summary:
Chakra is an intelligent agricultural recommendation platform designed to optimize decision-making in the agricultural sector by fusing NASA Earth observation data (POWER, MODIS/VIIRS), real-time telemetry captured by IoT devices, and reference agronomic knowledge bases (FAO ECOCROP and INIAP).

For field monitoring, the system integrates high-precision edaphic and environmental sensors that continuously measure critical variables such as soil macronutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium — NPK), ambient humidity, air temperature, wind speed/direction, site-accumulated precipitation, and local solar radiation. This information is transmitted via wireless communication technologies (such as Wi-Fi or cellular networks), enabling users to visualize and monitor the status of their crops in real time from any device.

Powered by machine learning algorithms such as XGBoost (eXtreme Gradient Boosting) and Explainable AI (XAI) techniques using SHAP (which ensure continuous calibration and correction with each iteration), Chakra analyzes the climatic, edaphic, and predictive conditions of the land. The result is a decision-support system that provides farmers and technical teams with precise recommendations on the rotation and selection of the next 3 ideal crops to maximize productivity and soil sustainability.
details:
Our project integrates two technological solutions: a low-cost weather station and ChakrIA, an artificial intelligence system designed to improve agricultural decision-making.

Developed by our team, the station measures air temperature, relative humidity, solar radiation, precipitation, wind speed, wind direction, soil nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and soil moisture. Powered by solar energy, it transmits data through WiFi or LoRa in areas without internet access.

ChakrIA analyzes eight years of NASA POWER satellite data and technical guidelines from FAO and INIAP to recommend suitable crops based on local agroclimatic conditions.

Our innovation combines satellite information with real field measurements. When both sources agree, ChakrIA validates its recommendations; when discrepancies occur, it adjusts them and generates alerts. Farmers receive three crop alternatives, a crop rotation plan, and understandable explanations supporting each recommendation.

The solution is affordable, replicable, energy-independent, and capable of storing data offline. It incorporates ESP32, Heltec LoRa, environmental and soil sensors, C++ (Arduino), KiCad, Python, XGBoost, SHAP, FastAPI, and Docker.

By connecting space-based information with ground-level measurements through explainable artificial intelligence, our project addresses the economic, environmental, and connectivity challenges faced by Ecuadorian farmers, promoting more informed and sustainable agricultural decisions.
